# iliad-132 — new renderings (21.1–96)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἀλωή (21.36, ἐκ πατρὸς ἀλωῆς; the planted ground where Lycaon cut fig shoots) | "orchard" (his father’s orchard) | "orchard" | "garden", "plot" (kept for the Odyssey’s 24.221), "threshing-floor" (the table’s 5.499 and 20.496, where winnowing fixes that sense), "vineyard"; follows the table’s 5.90 / 6.293 "orchard" |
| ἐϋκτιμένῃ ἐν ἀλωῇ (21.77; the same orchard recalled by Lycaon) | "in the well-built orchard" | "in the well-tilled orchard" | "well-built threshing-floor" (20.496, a different sense of ἀλωή), "well-settled"; the `l` / `i` pair follows the Odyssey’s ἐϋκτιμένη ἀλωή (24.226) "well-built" / "well-tilled" |
| ἀνώϊστον κακόν (21.39; ἀ- + οἴομαι, "not expected") | "an unlooked-for evil" | "an unforeseen evil" | "unexpected", "unhoped-for", "unimagined" |
| ὁμογάστριος (21.95) | "of the same womb" | "from the same womb" (+ note: a full brother, same mother) | "brother by the same mother", "uterine", "full brother" (the Greek has no word for brother) |
| στρεπτοῖσι χιτῶσι (21.31) | "twisted tunics" | "twisted tunics" (+ note: what kind of tunic is not known) | "woven", "pliant", "close-fitting" (each picks a sense of στρεπτός) |
| εὐόρμου (λιμένος, 21.23) | "of good anchorage" | "with good anchorage" | "sheltered", "safe", "well-moored" |
| λύμην … πορών (21.80; aorist middle of λύω, old athematic form) | "I was ransomed, having given" | "I have been ransomed, paying" (+ note on the form) | "I paid my own ransom", "I was freed at a cost" |
| ἱεμένη χροὸς ἄμεναι ἀνδρομέοιο (21.70; the spear personified) | "eager to be sated on the flesh, a man’s" | "eager to glut itself on human flesh" | "hungry for", "longing to taste"; ἄμεναι is the infinitive of ἄω "sate" |
| ἑλισσόμενοι (21.11) · εἰλεῦντο (21.8) | "turning" · "were crowded" | "turning round" · "were crowded" | "whirling" (kept for the table’s ἑλισσομένη "curling about", 1.317 and the like), "herded", "driven" |
| καί μιν φωνήσας ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (21.73; departure from iliad-002 at 1.201 in the pronoun only) | "and, lifting his voice, to him winged words he spoke:" | "and lifting his voice he spoke winged words to him:" | "to her" (the published English of 1.201, where μιν is Athena; here μιν is Achilles); follows the Odyssey’s departures at 4.312 and 4.369 |

Reused without change from the tables, listed for the reviewer: ποδάρκης δῖος Ἀχιλλεύς "swift-footed, heavenly Achilles"; τὸν δ’ ὡς οὖν ἐνόησε "Him then as he noticed" / "And when … noticed him"; γουνοῦμαί σ’ … αἴδεο καί μ’ ἐλέησον (22.312 pattern, Achilles for Odysseus); ἐπιστροφάδην "turning from one to another" / "wheeling from one man to the next"; στόνος ἀεικής "unseemly groaning"; ἀκάματον πῦρ "untiring fire"; ἐρινεός "wild fig-tree"; ἔσθορε "leapt in"; ἀτυζόμενοι "dazed with fear"; μεγακήτης "huge"; ἐπιμίξ "in confusion"; διογενής "Zeus-sprung" / "Zeus-born"; δαίμονι ἶσος "equal to a divinity" / "like a divinity"; ἠερέθονται "are fluttering"; μοῖρ’ ὀλοή "the deadly fate"; τρὶς τόσσα "thrice as much"; φρεσί "wits" (21.19, 21.61; 21.94 keeps the published "mind"); δειροτομέω "cut the throat of"; ἑκατόμβοιος "worth a hundred oxen"; ἀλφάνω "bring in".

Published-unit identities honoured: 21.53 (= 11.403) and 21.94 (= 1.297) are whole units with the published English. 21.1–2 reuses the published wording of 14.433–434 line for line. 21.54 reuses the published first line (13.99) with its ending adapted to the new context.
